PAPERS.short: Deng ultrafine particles kidney disease ED visits New York 2026
PAPERS.title: A mysterious danger for kidney disease exacerbations: short-term impacts of ultrafine particles on hospital visits
PAPERS.pm: Daily UFP number concentration from a validated chemical transport model (street-geocoded residence)
PAPERS.endpoint: Emergency department visits with a principal kidney-disease diagnosis
PAPERS.n: New York State discharge data 2013-2018 (95% of hospitals), 269,945 kidney-disease ED visits, conditional logistic regression per IQR of modelled UFP. Associations appeared at lag 1 and on every cumulative lag 0-1 to 0-6, peaking at lag 0-3: excess risk 0.74% (0.28-1.20) per IQR. Larger in adults >65, non-African American patients, hot and dry days, and fall/winter. Limitation: UFP is a CTM product, not a measurement; its spatial error is large and likely correlated with PM2.5 and NO2, and the abstract reports no co-pollutant adjustment, so 'UFP-specific' toxicity is not isolated. The effect per IQR is small. Relevance: high - a state-scale UFP health signal built entirely on modelled number concentration is the case for CPC or OPC-extended nodes to validate it.

PAPERS.short: Yuksel COPD cigarette biomass combined exposure exacerbations Turkiye 2026
PAPERS.title: Clinical outcomes of COPD associated with cigarette smoke, biomass smoke, and combined exposure: A retrospective observational study
PAPERS.pm: Household biomass smoke (fuel type and duration from records); no PM measurement
PAPERS.endpoint: COPD exacerbations, chronic respiratory failure, FEV1
PAPERS.n: 319 stable COPD patients: smoking-associated 159, biomass-associated 80, combined 80. Combined exposure presented younger (59.2 vs 61.4 and 63.5 y), with lower FEV1 (48% vs 55-56% predicted), more chronic respiratory failure (26.2% vs 17.0% and 11.2%) and, adjusted, severe exacerbations AOR 1.89 (1.22-2.96) vs smoking alone. Limitation: exposure is a retrospective chart classification with no dose for biomass, and the equal group sizes (80/80) suggest selection rather than consecutive enrolment. Pack-years differ by group and are not shown to be balanced, so 'combined' may simply mean heavier total exposure. Relevance: low - no measured particle exposure.

PAPERS.short: Holm CHAPS Fresno neurobehavior BDNF children air pollution 2026
PAPERS.title: Neurobehavioral assessments and biomarkers in school children who are highly exposed to air pollution
PAPERS.pm: Daily prenatal and first-year PM2.5, PM10, O3, NO2, NOx, PAH456 and EC
PAPERS.endpoint: NIH Toolbox cognition, CBCL behaviour, standardized test scores, serum BDNF, urinary 8-OHdG
PAPERS.n: Children's Health and Air Pollution Study, n=193 aged 7-18. Third-grade test scores correlated with NIH Toolbox total and crystallized composites (r 0.55-0.60) and with BDNF (r 0.35). First-trimester traffic pollutants were associated with aggressive and rule-breaking behaviour; first-year exposure to all pollutants with lower BDNF, window around 5-6 months. Limitation: 193 children, many pollutants, windows and outcomes, and no effect sizes or multiple-testing control in the abstract - the window findings are exploratory. Pollutants are highly collinear in Fresno, so 'all pollutants' cannot attribute the BDNF signal to PM or EC. Relevance: medium - EC and PAH contrasts again point to absorption channels rather than mass.

PAPERS.short: ICMR-SPIC stillbirth risk factors biomass fuel India pooled cohort 2026
PAPERS.title: Prevalence and risk factors for stillbirths in India: secondary analysis of ICMR-Stillbirth Pooled India Cohort (ICMR-SPIC)
PAPERS.pm: Household biomass fuel use (questionnaire); no PM measurement
PAPERS.endpoint: Stillbirth
PAPERS.n: Ten prospective pregnancy cohorts 1994-2023 harmonised, 227,821 pregnancies, 3,935 stillbirths; weighted rate 14.8/1000 (13.4-16.3). In mixed-effects modified Poisson models, biomass fuel use aIRR 1.37 (1.21-1.57) with the largest population attributable fraction of any factor, 13.95% (9.11-18.79), ahead of nulliparity and hypertensive disorders. Limitation: biomass use is a binary household marker strongly tied to rural residence, poverty and access to obstetric care; mutual adjustment for education does not remove that, so the PAF is an upper bound, not a smoke effect. Cohorts span three decades with different ascertainment. Relevance: low - the household-air-pollution burden case, without a particle metric.

PAPERS.short: Accra PM2.5 elemental composition PMF source shift e-waste burning 2026
PAPERS.title: Shifting Dominant Air Pollution Sources in Sub-Saharan Africa's Changing Urban Environment: Analysis of Elemental Composition and Source Contributions of Ambient Fine Particulate Matter (PM2.5) Pollution in Accra, Ghana
PAPERS.design: Intensive field campaign, PMF source apportionment
PAPERS.pm: Weekly gravimetric PM2.5 filters, ED-XRF elements, PMF
PAPERS.endpoint: Elemental composition and source contributions; decadal change at four legacy sites
PAPERS.n: Citywide campaign April 2019-June 2020: >600 weekly gravimetric PM2.5 filters from 146 sites, ED-XRF and PMF, compared with four legacy sites from 2007-2008. Harmattan crustal dust was 52-68% of elemental mass. Outside Harmattan, 4-6 factors: biomass burning 11-32%, traffic/road dust 9-36%, solid and e-waste combustion 0-35%. Over a decade the biomass contribution fell by ~16% (5.2-25.8) while waste burning rose by 23 points (15.9-30.0). Limitation: ED-XRF elements miss the carbonaceous fraction, so the shares are of elemental mass, not PM2.5 mass, and the decadal comparison rests on four sites. Relevance: high - a 146-site gravimetric network is the speciation reference a West African LCS network needs; e-waste burning is a source optical sensors cannot distinguish.

PAPERS.short: Julaha vertical aerosol chemical composition 230 m 4 m ACSM rural background 2026
PAPERS.title: Meteorological Effects on the Vertical Variability of Aerosol Chemical Composition at a Rural Background Site
PAPERS.pm: Submicron Org, SO4, NO3, NH4 (ToF-AMS at 230 m, ToF-ACSM at 4 m), eBC, OC/EC
PAPERS.endpoint: 230 m / 4 m concentration ratios by species, season and mixing height
PAPERS.n: Concurrent dual-height speciation, December 2019-May 2020: compact ToF-AMS at 230 m, ToF-ACSM at 4 m, Sunset OCEC. Every component was higher at 4 m; median 230/4 m ratios 0.55-0.82. Carbonaceous species had the steepest gradients and winter peaks; secondary inorganics were more homogeneous. Under inversions with mixing height <230 m, surface concentrations were 2-3x those aloft. Limitation: two different instruments at the two heights (AMS vs ACSM) - inter-instrument bias contributes directly to the ratio, and the abstract gives no co-location intercomparison. One site, one half-year. Relevance: high - a 2-3x surface/aloft contrast under shallow mixing is the bias any satellite-AOD or tower-based calibration of ground sensors must model.

PAPERS.short: Lu heterogeneous ammonia uptake SOA WRF-Chem North China Plain 2026
PAPERS.title: Impacts of the heterogeneous ammonia uptake on air quality in the North China Plain
PAPERS.pm: WRF-Chem PM2.5, inorganic aerosol and nitrogen-containing organics (NOCs)
PAPERS.endpoint: Change in NH3, inorganic aerosol, PM2.5 and NOCs
PAPERS.n: A first-order NH3 uptake on SOA forming NOCs was added to WRF-Chem for November 2017, with uptake coefficient gamma 1e-5 to 1e-3. Laboratory decline in reaction efficiency and measured NOC burdens support gamma=1e-5 as a conservative upper limit. At that value, NH3 fell 0.62%, inorganic aerosol and PM2.5 fell <0.06%, and the pathway produced 1.2 ug/m3 of NOCs. Limitation: one month, one region, and the constraining gamma is chosen partly from the NOC burden it is meant to explain. Relevance: low - a negligible PM2.5 mass term; useful only as a null for the chemistry.

PAPERS.short: Mandujano change-point detection trend estimation long-term PM records 2026
PAPERS.title: Assessing the Effect of Change-Point Detection Techniques on Trend Estimation in Long-Term Particulate Matter Records
PAPERS.pm: Long-term PM monitoring records
PAPERS.endpoint: PM trend estimates with and without change-point segmentation
PAPERS.n: Mandujano, Gonzalez, Hernandez, Guillen et al. Only the opening sentence of the abstract was retrievable from Crossref or Semantic Scholar: long-term PM trend analyses assume a single trend direction across the record, which can mask structural changes. The title states that change-point detection techniques are compared for their effect on trend estimates. Location, data set, methods and results are not available at harvest; nothing is inferred. Relevance: medium - instrument changes and station relocations are exactly the breakpoints that contaminate trends from mixed reference/LCS archives; retry the abstract.

PAPERS.short: zum Berge multicopter vibration optical particle counter accuracy 2026
PAPERS.title: Influence of multicopter-induced vibrations on the measurement accuracy of optical particle counter
PAPERS.pm: Optical particle counter size-resolved counts on a multicopter UAV
PAPERS.endpoint: OPC measurement accuracy under rotor-induced vibration
PAPERS.n: Title and authors only (zum Berge, Platis, Bange). No abstract was retrievable from Crossref or Semantic Scholar at harvest. The title describes quantifying how airframe vibration from a multicopter degrades the accuracy of an optical particle counter carried aloft - relevant to the growing use of drone-borne OPCs (often the same Alphasense/Plantower-class sensors used in ground networks) for vertical PM profiling. Design, sensor model, vibration spectrum and error magnitudes are not available; nothing is inferred. Relevance: high - vibration is an uncharacterised error term for mobile and UAV-mounted low-cost OPCs; retry the abstract first.

PAPERS.short: Washeem machine learning condensation bioaerosol sampler collection volume 2026
PAPERS.title: Machine-Learning-Guided Prediction and Temperature Optimization for Collection Volume Control in a Condensation-Based Bioaerosol Sampler
PAPERS.pm: Bioaerosol (condensation-growth liquid collection)
PAPERS.endpoint: Collection-volume prediction and temperature set-point optimisation
PAPERS.n: Title and authors only (Washeem, Li, Jansen, Shirkhani et al.). No abstract was retrievable at harvest. The title describes using machine learning to predict and control the liquid collection volume of a condensation-growth bioaerosol sampler by optimising its temperature set points. Instrument, training data and performance are not available; nothing is inferred. Relevance: low - sampler control engineering for bioaerosol, adjacent to but outside mass-concentration sensing.

PAPERS.short: Vannini biochar passive biomonitor potentially toxic elements lichens 2026
PAPERS.title: Wood-derived biochar as a potential sustainable alternative to lichens for monitoring airborne potentially toxic elements
PAPERS.pm: Airborne potentially toxic elements accumulated on exposed biochar
PAPERS.endpoint: Element uptake by biochar vs lichen biomonitors
PAPERS.n: Title and authors only (Vannini, Sidoli, Pagano, Magnani). No abstract was retrievable at harvest. The title proposes wood-derived biochar as a standardisable passive accumulator of airborne potentially toxic elements in place of transplanted lichens. Exposure design, elements, comparison data and agreement are not available; nothing is inferred. Relevance: medium - a cheap passive element sampler could add composition to dense optical-mass networks, provided uptake can be calibrated to air concentration.

PAPERS.short: Aktypis nucleation-mode particles marine atmosphere downwind urban 2026
PAPERS.title: Frequent Appearance of Nucleation-Mode Particles in the Marine Atmosphere Downwind of an Urban Area
PAPERS.pm: Nucleation-mode particle number size distributions
PAPERS.endpoint: Frequency of nucleation-mode particle appearance downwind of a city
PAPERS.n: Title and authors only (Aktypis, Vasilakopoulou, Matrali, Kaltsonoudis et al.). No abstract was retrievable at harvest. The title reports frequent nucleation-mode particles in marine air downwind of an urban area, implying urban plumes seed new-particle formation or carry fresh emissions over water. Site, instrumentation and event statistics are not available; nothing is inferred. Relevance: low - sub-25 nm particles are invisible to optical sensors and carry negligible mass.

PAPERS.short: Blanco-Alegre ironing indoor ultrafine particles ventilation eBC 2026
PAPERS.title: Ironing as a Source of Indoor Aerosol Particles: Effects of Ventilation and Ironing Conditions
PAPERS.pm: Particle number concentration and size distribution, eBC
PAPERS.endpoint: PNC, PNSD, eBC and particle emission rates during ironing
PAPERS.n: Residential measurements with a conventional steam iron and a steam iron with a portable boiler, at low and higher ventilation. PNC rose by about two orders of magnitude during ironing, mostly 20-80 nm, to a maximum of 7.12e5 cm-3 (conventional iron, low ventilation). Emission rates 8.1e11-1.5e12 particles/min, highest for the boiler iron at low ventilation; modes shifted to larger sizes after ironing; eBC changed little. Limitation: one dwelling, few repetitions, and the source mechanism (water additives, fabric, soleplate heating) is not separated; no mass concentration is reported, so health relevance is by number only. Relevance: medium - an ultrafine source that optical home sensors will undercount almost entirely.

PAPERS.short: Ruengdit active-flow respirator fit children Chiang Mai 2026
PAPERS.title: Active-flow systems enhance respirator fit success in children: a comparative study with standard disposable models
PAPERS.pm: Quantitative fit factor (TSI PortaCount, ambient particle counting)
PAPERS.endpoint: Respirator fit pass rate (overall fit factor >=100)
PAPERS.n: 82 children aged 5-10, modified OSHA quantitative fit test. A standard triple-fold KN95-equivalent FFR passed in 3.7%; adding a portable HEPA unit supplying 66.5 L/min positive pressure raised the pass rate to 23.2% (OR 17.0) and median fit factor from 9.5 to 39.5. Wider bizygomatic breadth (aOR 1.31) and longer menton-sellion (1.11) favoured fit; head nodding was worst. Limitation: no CI given for the OR; crossover order and fit-test learning effects are not described, and 77% still failed with the active system. Relevance: high - a median fit factor of 9.5 means adult masks give children roughly 90% leakage-limited protection at best, which matters for exposure-reduction advice issued from LCS haze alerts.

PAPERS.short: Donohoe ultrafine amorphous silica epithelial stress pro-fibrotic 2026
PAPERS.title: Ultrafine amorphous silica induces chronic epithelial cell stress and pro-fibrotic reprogramming in a particle size- and exposure duration-dependent manner
PAPERS.pm: Ultrafine amorphous silica particles
PAPERS.endpoint: Epithelial stress and pro-fibrotic reprogramming
PAPERS.n: Title and authors only (Donohoe, Selvamani, Dharwal, O'Neil et al.). No abstract was retrievable at harvest. The title reports that ultrafine amorphous silica causes chronic epithelial cell stress and pro-fibrotic reprogramming that depends on particle size and exposure duration - relevant because amorphous silica is usually treated as low-hazard relative to crystalline silica. Model system, doses and endpoints are not available; nothing is inferred. Relevance: low - toxicology of a particle class not resolved by mass sensors.

PAPERS.short: Zhao coal dust macrophage extracellular vesicles thyroid cancer miR-205-5p 2026
PAPERS.title: Coal dust-stimulated macrophage-derived extracellular vesicles promote thyroid cancer cell phenotypes involving miR-205-5p, CAMK1G, and NF-kB-associated signaling
PAPERS.pm: Characterised coal dust (macrophage exposure; murine exposure)
PAPERS.endpoint: Thyroid cancer cell viability, migration, invasion; xenograft growth
PAPERS.n: THP-1 macrophages exposed to characterised coal dust released extracellular vesicles enriched in miR-205-5p; these increased TPC-1 thyroid cancer cell viability, clonogenicity, migration and invasion and reduced apoptosis. Effects ran through CAMK1G and NF-kB (p65, IkBa phosphorylation) and were attenuated by miR-205-5p inhibition or CAMK1G knockdown; coal-dust-exposed mice and humanised xenograft mice were used in vivo. Limitation: the premise - coal dust promoting thyroid cancer - has no epidemiological anchor, and macrophage dosing in vitro is far above realistic lung burdens. Relevance: low - occupational mechanism without an exposure metric.

PAPERS.journal: J Toxicol Environ Health B Crit Rev
PAPERS.short: Wang PM2.5 lung cancer nonsmokers narrative review IL-1beta EGFR screening 2026
PAPERS.title: Environmental PM2.5 exposure associated with lung cancer in nonsmokers: a narrative review of high-risk groups, mechanisms, and implications for screening
PAPERS.pm: Ambient and microenvironmental PM2.5 (incense, cooking, transit, occupational)
PAPERS.endpoint: Lung cancer in never-smokers; screening eligibility
PAPERS.n: Narrative review of cohort, meta-analytic and toxicological evidence on PM2.5 and lung cancer in never-smokers (<100 lifetime cigarettes), weighted to East Asian women. Emphasises macrophage IL-1beta signalling promoting EGFR-mutant adenocarcinoma, and lists high-exposure microenvironments: incense burning, cooking and solid fuel, subway/bus/motorbike commuting and professional driving, firefighting, construction, informal e-waste recycling. Argues for cumulative PM2.5 in risk-prediction models and screening of exposed never-smokers. Limitation: non-systematic; no new quantitative synthesis, and the microenvironment list is not dose-ranked. Relevance: medium - cumulative personal PM2.5 as a screening criterion would need exactly the personal and microenvironment data wearable sensors produce.

PAPERS.short: Shi air pollution pulmonary tuberculosis incidence China GTWR 2026
PAPERS.title: Analysis of influencing factors of atmospheric pollution on pulmonary tuberculosis incidence in China from 2014 to 2020
PAPERS.pm: Provincial annual PM2.5, SO2, NO2, CO, O3
PAPERS.endpoint: Pulmonary tuberculosis incidence
PAPERS.n: Provincial panel 2014-2020 (31 units), spatial autocorrelation, space-time scanning and geographically and temporally weighted regression (R2 0.889), with 1-5-year moving-average exposure windows. High-burden clusters persisted in Xinjiang, Xizang and Qinghai (RR 3.56). PM2.5 coefficients ran 'east-negative, west-positive'; SO2, NO2 and CO were jointly positive in the north-east; O3 mostly negative. Limitation: 217 province-years and locally varying coefficients amount to a flexible fit of an ecological surface; the sign flip of PM2.5 across China shows confounding by development and TB control, not toxicity. Relevance: low.

PAPERS.short: Imman caregivers PM2.5 prevention preschool children northern Thailand qualitative 2026
PAPERS.title: Caregivers' experiences of PM2.5 prevention for preschool children in Thailand: a qualitative study with focus group interviews
PAPERS.pm: Seasonal haze PM2.5 (perceived); no measurement
PAPERS.endpoint: Caregiver perceptions and protective practices
PAPERS.n: Focus groups plus in-depth interviews with 20 primary caregivers (14 women) of preschool children in a rural northern Thai community subject to recurrent haze; content analysis (Graneheim and Lundman). Themes: barriers of awareness and responsibility against pervasive local sources; individual prevention driven by visible symptoms rather than air-quality information; and a shift toward collective action and calls for structural change (waste-burning control). Limitation: one community, 20 participants, no link to measured exposure or behaviour change. Relevance: medium - caregivers act on symptoms, not data; local sensor displays only help if they reach this audience in an actionable form.

PAPERS.journal: Int J Occup Med Environ Health
PAPERS.short: Grzesczyk-Nojszewska Poland air pollution interventions public attitudes survey 2026
PAPERS.title: Public attitudes toward personal and population interventions to reduce air pollution exposure: a 2025 nationwide cross-sectional survey in Poland
PAPERS.pm: Air pollution (perceived); no measurement
PAPERS.endpoint: Attitudes to personal and population exposure-reduction measures
PAPERS.n: CAWI survey, May 2025, quota sample of 1,092 adults. 76.4% saw air pollution as requiring public action (women aOR 1.47, 1.11-1.96; age >=60 aOR 2.49, 1.59-3.91). Commonest protective behaviours: closing windows during episodes (44.2%) and avoiding outdoor time (36.5%). Fines for burning prohibited materials in home furnaces had 70.2% support. Limitation: quota online panels over-represent the engaged; no link to local concentrations, and stated behaviours are unverified. Relevance: medium - window closing is the dominant action, so indoor/outdoor paired sensing is what tells people whether it works.

PAPERS.short: Mohamadi Isfahan PM2.5 AirQ+ WRF-SMOKE-CMAQ health damage 2026
PAPERS.title: Assessing the health impacts of PM2.5 from anthropogenic and natural sources in Isfahan, Iran
PAPERS.pm: Monitoring-station annual PM2.5; WRF-SMOKE-CMAQ source contributions
PAPERS.endpoint: Monetised PM2.5 health damage (AirQ+)
PAPERS.n: Station annual PM2.5 fed AirQ+; at a 2020 GDP of USD 2,283 per capita, annual health damage was USD 441 M (253-628 M). A year-long WRF-SMOKE-CMAQ run attributed 7.9% of damage to iron and steel, 2.2% to cement and 1.7% to brick kilns; 'environmental' (natural) particles accounted for USD 115.3 M (26%). Limitation: attributing damage linearly by modelled mass share assumes equal toxicity, and the share of dust (natural) depends on how the inventory handles anthropogenic fugitive dust. Few stations in a large city. Relevance: low - a standard AirQ+ exercise; denser monitoring would mainly tighten the exposure input.

PAPERS.short: Szczepanik Warsaw wintertime air quality improvement 2016-2025 2026
PAPERS.title: Improvement in wintertime air quality in urban and suburban areas of Warsaw within 2016-2025
PAPERS.pm: Wintertime ambient air quality (pollutants not stated)
PAPERS.endpoint: Decadal change in wintertime air quality, urban vs suburban
PAPERS.n: Title and authors only (Szczepanik, Deptula, Klapinski, Rakowska). No abstract was retrievable at harvest. The title reports improved wintertime air quality across urban and suburban Warsaw over 2016-2025, the period of Poland's anti-smog resolutions and boiler-replacement programmes. Pollutants, data sources and magnitudes are not available; nothing is inferred. Relevance: medium - suburban solid-fuel heating is where Polish LCS networks (Airly and others) are densest; the paper may use them.
